editorial:
Imagine waking up in the middle of nowhere with no idea who you are, but you happen to be an expert with a gun. That is exactly where you start with Noon. You get to follow this mysterious guy as he teams up with Rimes, a friendly outlaw who helps him piece together his broken memory. The vibe is a classic dusty Western, but with a cool mystery twist. As you watch, you find out that Noon has a tragic past involving his family and a hidden stash of money. You will feel for him as he tries to find the truth while dodging bad people who want him dead.

What really makes this work is the tension between the lead characters and the greedy villains, like the judge and Peg. The action is solid and the mystery keeps you guessing until the end. It is not the fastest movie, but the slow build makes the payoffs feel better. If you are a fan of old-school shootouts, you should definitely check this out. Since it is an older film, you might want to grab the 4K Blu-ray for your physical collection to get the best picture quality, or just rent it on Apple TV for a quick movie night.
endingExplained: In the final act, Noon finally remembers everything and finds the hidden money. The greedy judge and Peg try to steal it and kill him, but Noon uses his gunfighting skills to take them down in a big shootout. After clearing out the villains, Noon finds some peace. He leaves the life of violence behind and heads off with Fan Davidge, finally free from the ghosts of his past and the people hunting him.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves classic Westerns with a mystery twist.
